newsitem.title: INDIA: Eight policemen wounded in Kashmir grenade attack.
newsitem.headline: Eight policemen wounded in Kashmir grenade attack.

text.p: Eight policemen were wounded in Kashmir on Tuesday when suspected separatist guerrillas lobbed a grenade at a government minister's escort vehicle, police said.

They said the vehicle, which caught fire and was destroyed, had been travelling near a crowded marketplace in the heart of Srinagar after dropping the state's junior revenue minister, Safdar Ali Beigh, at his residence.
Police said pedestrians were also wounded in the blast. They gave no further details.

Last week a landmine planted by separatist guerrillas in Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir, killed a police official and wounded at least eight people, including five police personnel.
More than a dozen militant groups are waging a separatist rebellion in Jammu and Kashmir, mainly Hindu India's only Moslem-majority province.
Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have been killed since the revolt in the Himalayan region erupted in 1990.
